name: websearch-mcp-cli

tools.name: academicsearch
tools.description:
Academic paper search: queries several scholarly databases in parallel and returns standardized Markdown results (title, authors, DOI, venue, citation count, PDF link).

Available engines (the engines parameter accepts several; empty means all):
  - crossref: Crossref scholarly metadata (all fields, with DOI/citations)
  - openalex: OpenAlex open scholarly graph (all fields, with citation counts/relevance score)
  - pubmed: PubMed biomedical literature (medicine/life sciences)
  - europepmc: Europe PMC biomedical/life sciences (PubMed supplement, with citation counts)
  - dblp: DBLP computer science literature (CS conference/journal index)
  - doaj: DOAJ open access journals (open access papers across all fields)
  - arxiv: arXiv preprints (CS/physics/math)

Engine guidance: medicine/biology → pubmed, europepmc | CS/AI → arxiv, semantic_scholar, dblp | all fields → crossref, openalex, google_scholar | open access → doaj

When you already have a DOI or arXiv id, pass it directly as query (e.g. '10.1038/s41586-020-2649-2', 'doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2649-2', 'https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2649-2' or '2401.04085', 'arXiv:2401.04085', 'https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.04085'); this performs an exact single-paper lookup (still honoring registered or explicitly requested engines; time_range and page do not apply). Given a pdf_url in the result, pass that URL as the path parameter of the pdf_parser tool to parse the full text.

Scope: papers, preprints and DOI-level scholarly lookup; for news, product docs and other general web information use smartsearch instead.

project.description: Optional project statistics label: fill in only a project short name already established in the current context (Chinese is supported); omit it when unknown, do not send paths, do not guess from the query, and do not ask the user for it. Used for statistics only; it does not affect search or fetch.

query.description: Academic search keywords, for example 'transformer attention mechanism' or 'CRISPR gene editing'

engines.description: Specify a subset of engines (empty uses every enabled engine). Examples: ["pubmed"] for medical papers, ["arxiv"] for CS preprints, ["arxiv","crossref"] for physics/math

time_range.description: Time range filter. Options: year (last year), month (last month), week (last week), day (last day). Empty means no limit

page.description: Result page number (default 1); roughly 10 results per page

tools.name: cleanfetch
tools.description: Full-text retrieval tool. url/urls fetch web pages as Markdown (merged and deduplicated, up to 5); alternatively pass a result_ref returned by another tool to read saved search, web or PDF text in segments, returning content, next_offset and eof without re-requesting the source. The two modes are mutually exclusive; offset/limit apply only to reference reads. Always registered; cleanfetch.enabled controls URL fetching only. Use smartsearch first to discover sources.

project.description: Optional project statistics label: fill in only a project short name already established in the current context (Chinese is supported); omit it when unknown, do not send paths, do not guess from the query, and do not ask the user for it. Used for statistics only; it does not affect search or fetch.

url.description: Web page URL to fetch, for example 'https://example.com/article'; cannot be combined with result_ref

urls.description: Optional batch fetch: merged and deduplicated with url, up to 5. Each URL is pre-checked and fetched independently, one failure does not affect the others, and results are returned in per-URL sections

result_ref.description: Read content already saved by this service; only accepts a result_ref returned by another tool, never a path or URL; mutually exclusive with url/urls

offset.description: Only for result_ref: 0-based Unicode character offset; use next_offset to continue reading

limit.description: Only for result_ref: characters per segment; omitted or 0 means 4096, max 8192

tools.name: smartsearch
tools.description: General-purpose web search for real-time information (news, technical docs, products, data). Keep the query focused and precise; piling up synonyms and secondary terms into a keyword list dilutes relevance. Use fetch_top_n to fetch the full text of the top N scored results (default 0 = no fetch, max 5). Falls back to Bing when the primary engine is unavailable. Scope: time-sensitive facts, web leads and document lookup; for systematic literature reviews or academic questions that need citations, use academicsearch instead.

project.description: Optional project statistics label: fill in only a project short name already established in the current context (Chinese is supported); omit it when unknown, do not send paths, do not guess from the query, and do not ask the user for it. Used for statistics only; it does not affect search or fetch.

query.description: Search keywords: express the core intent precisely and concisely (2-6 keywords or one short phrase recommended), keeping only the terms that best pin down the target. Do not pile synonyms, process words and modifiers into a keyword list, which dilutes relevance. For example use 'Go generics performance' rather than 'Go generics type parameters compile runtime performance benchmark comparison optimization usage'.

time_range.description: Search time range in months, limiting results to the last N months. For example 1 = last month, 3 = last 3 months, 6 = last 6 months, 12 = last year. Defaults to 3; 0 means no limit.

fetch_top_n.description: Full-text fetch mode: when omitted, behavior matches older versions and only engine/provider-supplied content is returned (the server-side smartsearch.fetch_top_n can change the default, which is 0 = no fetch). 0 returns titles, snippets and URLs only; 1-5 fetches the page text of the top N results — API engines that accept full text take a fast path, other engines fetch the page internally. Results blocked by anti-bot protection (JS challenge/WAF) are annotated.
